admission.justification: Reusing a conversion without exact inputs could silently compare another code/memory baseline; the mismatch matrix protects reuse while avoiding repeated materialization of an already held tree.

applicability: Live tree comparisons whose before memory is converted from a legacy base.
conditions: The latest comparison record binds the same memory commit, pinned conversion version and paired code commit.
git cat-file confirms the recorded root object is a tree before reuse.
exclusions: A missing tree or mismatched conversion inputs retains the existing conversion/materialization behavior.
This does not skip capture of either live candidate or replace recorded comparison numbering and pins.

evidence: requirements/MIK-R40-v2-reviewer-read-latency-on-git-trees.md rule 3; exact post-B1 source notes/reports/260928-MIK-L40-worker-R2-evidence/final-2026-10-03/candidate-reader-post-b1.json sha256:ff7a5201d4ed37a6d2e109d9a8d3b9374adbd5f44009b7e7f686274ed218b6b2; independent R1/R2 plus notes/reports/260928-MIK-L40-review-R3.md (SHA-256 c9a9ea931c18de68182a0f1f12d57cc7e72d29358ed463328ce3d11ca3c988fd); phase-specific performance evidence remains pending

statement: A converted base tree is written only when Git does not hold it.
